Maybe interesting to some - I'll post this on the site on my team page too.  Also, showing how you can build a team in LL6 if you can ID talent, even if you join a team in mid season (it was day 23 in this case). For anyone who didn't read or wasn't around when I took them on read the press release here for more info: http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/team/437 I've stuck to points 1-3 which are the important 3 restrictions on the players I go for.  In position order only:  - El Nadi, http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/140578  combo guard with the "no perimeter defence" comment, had the most development in college of the 5 (+77 SI) that negative comment wasn't much of an issue in the end, and his current skills are about the top of what you could've projected. 1653 points (14th all-time for W-P), 672 assists (5th) and 230 steals (4th).  - Bellan, http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/127336  one of the best defenders I've had on any team. Efficient, but definitely a 5th offensive option so no outstanding stats, just 206 steals (7th)
[2022-12-15 18:14] bergkamp7349 : - Webber, http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/123649  great shooter, almost as good as defender as Bellan, super stamina so just locked down the SF position for 30+ minutes a game when needed. 2639 points (1st), 505 3 pointers at 40% (1st in both stats), 311 steals (1st), 32 POTGs (4th) - Wagoner, http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/126864  his flaw is the strength + speed but it was fine for LL5 & 6 at PF in the end. Does everything else you'd want a big to do. 2596 points (2nd), 1561 rebounds (2nd), 38 POTGs (2nd), 195 blocks (6th). Final FG% over 60% - McFadden, http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/125915  just a very large man, if only he could rebound a little better...rubbish development too (9 potential, but 31 total was still poor). 2520 points (3rd), 245 blocks (1st), 1153 rebounds (9th), 25 POTGs (6th). Final FG% almost 65%.   The odd man out was Andy Rees. http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/141318 7'0 with a 7'7 wingspan, but I barely used him after his SO year (that RS year was a mistake I was almost sure I was making at the time), the other 2 bigs then JR Daniel took the majority of minutes.  Total # of recruiting points: 34. 8 Rees, 6 McFadden, Bellan & El Nadi, 4 Webber & Wagoner.  I do feel I got a bit lucky with the players available that season, but I don't know - I've not tried the same experiment in the same way since.

[2022-12-19 04:03] lynxvj : Do you get better RPI winning against #1000-ranked opponent or losing against #1-ranked opponent?
[2022-12-19 04:56] furysk : not that i know what the exact formula is, but strength of schedule goes up with the #1 ranked team versus down with the #1000, so that would probably help you
[2022-12-19 05:08] slickandjakenillinois : https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/595769726597070869/1052422561314644058/image.png
[2022-12-19 05:10] slickandjakenillinois : Here are the formulas.  The RPI takes your opponent’s win percentage times 0.50 but your own win percentage just 0.25.  So it is about twice as better to lose to the #1 team than to win against the #1000, although not exactly.  The #1 team would have to have a 1.000 win percentage and the #1000 team a 0 win percentage, so it is less than 2 times better.  But hopefully you get the picture.
[2022-12-19 05:41] slickandjakenillinois : Let’s put it this way, let’s assume you have a win percentage of 0.800 against teams that have a win percentage of 0.200.  Let’s also assume your opponent’s opponent win percentage (OOWP) is 0.500.  Your RPI would be 0.425.  Now let’s say the opposite, your win percentage is 0.200 against teams with a win percentage of 0.800 and keeping the OOWP the same at 0.500.  Your RPI would be 0.575.  So it is better for your RPI to lose against high win percentage teams versus win against low win percentage teams.

[2022-12-26 07:14] naph7777 : Its an annoying "feature".  Basically if your assistant coach has ever been a head coach at any league level, then when he signs with you his salary gets reassessed based on your team's league level. As best I can tell it becomes the same as he would have had if he was your head coach.  IMO its a bug, but I've raised it with admin Steve and he hasn't done anything with it for multiple seasons now. So its now one of those "buyer beware" issues. Basically I now try and remember to avoid any coach that has ever been a head coach when I'm looking for assistant.  http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/forum/0/5/1783

[2023-02-07 01:12] naph7777 : I didn't always think it worked like this. But my current understanding of the Inside/Outside Emphasis does is:  O - run the ball through your PG. o - run the ball through your SG. ~ - run the ball through your SF. i - run the ball through your PF. I - run the ball through your C.   I used to think that it would be where all of your players on the court would be trying to score the ball more. (ie that if I had PF's and C's set to O, that they would get more shots if I set Inside/Outside Emphasis set to O)... but that doesn't seem to match what happens in games.
[2023-02-07 02:28] naph7777 : I do think it still works out so that if you're running it through your PG your SG still gets more touches than your C. If you run it through your SF, then your SG and PF get more touches than your PG/C etc.

If I set my PG to ++ and 'O' but offensive strategy at 'I' I think it just means he is going to take a lot of 3 point shots.  If he decides to not shoot it then he will try to pass it inside.

[2023-03-25 14:23] slickandjakenillinois : My opinion is that rating plays a huge part in the rankings.  And typically the higher conferences has teams with higher ratings.  There are obviously other variables, and I forget them all, I am pretty sure TPI has some factor in it as well.  But it becomes more obvious at the beginning of a season when no games are played and looking at the ranked teams.  The rating at that time is heavily weighted as numerous Legends teams litter the top 25 and the teams not in Legends but ranked have the higher TPIs.  And you will see no teams below D1.  As time goes on, either RPI, WP, SOS, or some combination probably adds into the mix.  Also interesting the point differential seems to play a part too.  After that first game teams in the Top 25 at the same league level that win will move up and down based on the point differential of their games, and everyone at that point has the same RPI, SOS, and WP so those variables don’t yet factor in.  So over time the lower division teams with a huge PD may creep into the rankings.

For the Musketeers, the lone bright spot was the performance of C Welch who finished with a double-double. On the other hand, the Panthers' star player SG Kenny Wright was unstoppable, finishing with a game-high 20 points, 11 rebounds,  six assists, and 3 steals. Wright was a nightmare matchup for Xavier. C Pruitt dominated the paint, finishing with 18 points, 14 rebounds, two steals, and two blocks. Pruitt made his presence felt on both ends of the floor, scoring in the post and protecting the rim on defense.  In the end, the Panthers played with energy and intensity from start to finish, while the Musketeers looked tired and outmatched. With the series tied at 1-1 this season, the Musketeers will need to regroup and find a way to bounce back from the disappointing loss.

[2023-08-02 17:35] lassoball : An under-appreciated problem with the old system was that legitimate and illegitimate transactions looked the same on their face.  For instance, I was one of the users who reported a pair of clearly fraudulent coaching transactions between two teams where both presidents were eventually removed.  Later on, I myself lucked into a great coach who just hit the open market, but he was so good that I ended up preemptively messaging Steve to flag it for his attention and let him know there was no collusion involved.  Since I used to check the coaching wire every hour around the flip, I snapped him up first, but had no prior knowledge he’d become available and since he was replaced with an average coach, the transaction would have appeared just as fraudulent, which compelled me to message Steve and ask him to confirm the transaction was acceptable.     Point is, I loved the mad scramble of the old system, but it also had room for abuse and, in some cases, there wasn’t even a way for people to tell the difference between those acting in good or bad faith.

[2023-11-09 19:54] fatherborf : also am i crazy or is there a seemingly large jump between the growth of most 11pot players and 12pot? i feel like ive gotta be a lot more strict on recruiting minimum 12 pot for most positions, the growth difference ive seen between 12pots and 10-11pots has been nuts
[2023-11-09 20:10] gards710 : lol you're not crazy. The average 12 pot has a higher ceiling than 11 or 10 pots. The average 12 pot also has better dev than the average 10 or 11 pot. But I wouldn't strictly recruit minimum 12 pots just because of that. As many of us have said, it's not about the potential or the SI or the number of stars. It's about all of those in combination with the "build" of the player. SI points in the right skills, with the right growth and high enough ceiling in those skills.
[2023-11-09 20:13] fatherborf : is my understanding that "bigs" also *generally* seem to have lower SIs/less SI growth than their guard counterparts? not in every case obviously but even at DIII i notice lots of decent bigs that make up for "low skills" with, like you say, having skills in the places that matter and having good measurables, like long wing spans and good height and weight
[2023-11-09 20:17] gards710 : bigs don't inherently have their skills in the right places, but yes, they usually will have less SI and slower development, simply because there are less skills that important to big men than there are for perimeter players, at least in theory. and yeah, the size helps make up for that

[2023-12-02 20:40] gards710 : Gards' usual answer without an answer incoming: it seems like you know basketball somewhat based on where you have some of your players playing, so that's good to get out of the way. Your tactics are going to depend on your goals because that will influence who should be getting minutes and thus the strengths and weaknesses of the personnel on the floor. Are you going to try and focus on winning this season or give minutes to younger players to develop more and be more competitive in the future? Ideally, it's both right? But that's rarely the case. In addition, focusing on the short term might have you trying tactics that you don't like using, so you have to answer what type of team you want to be (and then recruit players that fit that). My answer to this type of question is usually this: play around with different stuff and see what works in different situations and also what you like. My style of play is unique and I wouldn’t want to unduly influence someone else to play like that and there are several other ways to be successful in this game.
[2023-12-02 20:50] mattgcoot : With your current team I'd try a slower pace give starters a few less minutes and maybe less pressure.  Since I'm someone that likes to avoid heavy fatigue on players.  Your first couple of seasons i wouldn't worry too much on winning (at least I didn't) just try and focus on how the game works and just start trying different tactics every couple of games just to see the various results.  Then you can start recruiting players who you think can play in a system that you want to run.
